title: Record 158 Million Shoppers Expected During Super Saturday

facts.fact: More than 158 million consumers were expected to shop on Super Saturday (the last Saturday before Christmas) in 2022, according to NRF and Prosper Insights & Analytics.
facts.quote: More than 158 million consumers are expected to shop on the last Saturday before Christmas this year, according to the annual survey released today by the National Retail Federation and Prosper Insights & Analytics.

facts.fact: The expected Super Saturday shopper count was approximately 10 million more than the prior year's expected number, and the highest since NRF began tracking in 2016.
facts.quote: This figure is approximately 10 million more than last year’s expected number of Super Saturday shoppers and the highest number since NRF first started tracking this data in 2016.

facts.fact: Of the 158.5 million anticipated Super Saturday shoppers, 44.1 million (28%) planned to shop only in stores.
facts.quote: Of the 158.5 million anticipated Super Saturday shoppers, 44.1 million (28%) plan to shop only in stores

facts.fact: Of the 158.5 million anticipated Super Saturday shoppers, 42.2 million (27%) planned to shop only online.
facts.quote: 42.2 million (27%) plan to shop only online

facts.fact: Of the 158.5 million anticipated Super Saturday shoppers, 72.2 million (46%) planned to shop both in stores and online.
facts.quote: 72.2 million (46%) plan to shop both in stores and online.

facts.fact: As of early December 2022, holiday shoppers said they had completed about half (53%) of their purchases.
facts.quote: as of early December, holiday shoppers said they had completed about half (53%) of their purchases.

facts.fact: Holiday shoppers planned to finish their holiday purchases online (47%), at department stores (37%), at discount stores (27%), at clothing/accessories stores (24%), and at grocery stores (19%).
facts.quote: They plan to finish their holiday purchases online (47%), at department stores (37%), at discount stores (27%), at clothing/accessories stores (24%) and at grocery stores (19%).

facts.fact: The top gifts consumers had bought so far included clothing (50%), toys (34%), gift cards (28%), books and other media (26%), and food or candy (23%).
facts.quote: The top gifts consumers have bought so far include clothing (50%), toys (34%), gift cards (28%), books and other media (26%), and food or candy (23%).

facts.fact: 28% of holiday shoppers planned to give a gift of experience in 2022, up from 23% last year and the highest since NRF began asking in 2015.
facts.quote: This year, 28% of holiday shoppers plan to give a gift of experience... This is up from 23% last year and is the highest since NRF began asking consumers this question in 2015.

facts.fact: 70% of holiday shoppers said their shopping plans include buying after Dec. 25, on par with pre-pandemic levels for post-Christmas shopping.
facts.quote: Additionally, 70% say their shopping plans include buying after Dec. 25. This is on par with pre-pandemic levels for post-Christmas shopping.

facts.fact: About half (52%) of consumers say they are using alternative payments or digital wallets for holiday purchases, up from 44% last year.
facts.quote: About half (52%) of consumers say they are using alternative payments or digital wallets. This is up from 44% last year

facts.fact: Consumer use of alternative payments or digital wallets for holiday purchases was 39% in 2019.
facts.quote: compares with only 39% in 2019

facts.fact: The most common alternative payment method among holiday shoppers is PayPal, used by 32% of consumers.
facts.quote: The most common alternative payment is PayPal (32%)

facts.fact: Apple Pay is used by 14% of consumers as an alternative payment method during the holiday season.
facts.quote: followed by Apple Pay (14%) and CashApp (12%)

facts.fact: About three-quarters (76%) of consumers aged 18 to 24 say they have used an alternative payment method or digital wallet so far in the holiday shopping season.
facts.quote: About three-quarters (76%) of those aged 18 to 24 say they have used an alternative payment method

facts.fact: NRF defines the holiday season as Nov. 1 through Dec. 31.
facts.quote: NRF defines the holiday season as Nov. 1 through Dec. 31

facts.fact: NRF forecast that retail sales during the 2022 holiday season will grow between 6% and 8% over 2021 to between $942.6 billion and $960.4 billion.
facts.quote: retail sales will grow between 6% and 8% over 2021 to between $942.6 billion and $960.4 billion

facts.fact: The NRF holiday sales forecast projects holiday retail sales between $942.6 billion and $960.4 billion.
facts.quote: to between $942.6 billion and $960.4 billion

facts.fact: The Prosper Insights & Analytics survey covered 7,857 consumers and was conducted Dec. 1 through Dec. 7.
facts.quote: The survey of 7,857 consumers was conducted Dec. 1 through Dec. 7

facts.fact: The survey of 7,857 consumers has a margin of error of plus or minus 1.1 percentage points.
facts.quote: has a margin of error of plus or minus 1.1 percentage points

facts.fact: Retail contributes $3.9 trillion to annual GDP and supports one in four U.S. jobs, or 52 million working Americans, according to NRF.
facts.quote: contributing $3.9 trillion to annual GDP and supporting one in four U.S. jobs – 52 million working Americans
